cards.note: Ships as an npm bundle (dsh.bundle.patch) installed through the single official profile path `dsh plugin --profile <name> add @bench/dsh-bench-mcpanel`; no repository-plugins mechanism remains.
The manifest never declared the legacy dshClient field and ships no dsh.plugin.json; the packed manifest re-read from the tarball still carries dsh.client { platform: web }.
The web half declares dsh.client plus exports['./client'], so the scan finds it; the boot manifest carried the row and the combo route served it.
Every consumed service is declared (host inject ['tools']; client inject ['slots','locale']); no ctx.get or property access for an undeclared service.

The web-only webServer/connection services are no longer a hard inject: the host half keeps only tools (base-guaranteed) and records the weak ctx.get('webServer') probe so a non-web profile does not leave the fiber pending.
No session/event subscription and no session-state derivation anywhere in the tree.
The browser half consumes only slots and locale; there is no ctx.sessions or session aggregation to move to the Node half.
No task/run output tailing; neither tasks nor jobs is injected or read.
The tree already uses the post-rename webServer vocabulary and no httpServer/tasks/onTaskDone identifier remains.
No ImageAttachmentRef, read_image output or persisted image metadata in the plugin.
The plugin neither registers, wraps, parses nor snapshot-tests read_image.
No custom DeepSeek LLM adapter, image request interceptor or attachment cache.
Ordinary Cordis host plugin; it registers its own webServer routes and never touches the Host APIProxy.
Produces no persisted SessionEvents; target is alpha.2, where DSH-0.1.2-A2-01 owns the ignorable field.
No host source patch and no import from internal session-view paths.

The documented registry write side edits the active profile's own layer; the header now pins the runtime-DSH_HOME/profile path and keeps composition, package manifests and resolved config distinct (the elided body must resolve it that way).
No headless wrapper, stdout parser or stderr consumer in the plugin.
No tool-presentation mode, PTC preset or dispatch-waterfall usage.
Not a permission, approval, WebFetch-policy or audit plugin.

The custom /api/mcp-manager routes inherit neither the Connection gate nor the Host/Origin fence; the header records ctx.connection.requestRejection(req) per handler and the token->cookie rules (probe observed 303 + HttpOnly/SameSite=Strict cookie, then 200 on /).
Not a model-provider plugin; its 'MCP' entry is a settings.section row, not the model sign-in seat.
Localization already goes through the public ctx.locale.register/bind API with no custom i18n patch; the nav label now reads through the bound dictionary thunk.
No subagent orchestration or provider/model selector.
Informational deployment/adapter behavior; the plugin takes no official DeepSeek adapter dependency and needs no code change.
No PowerShell/Bash or Windows directory-picker compatibility workaround.
No session-log-deepseek egress, watermark or deployment privacy setting in the plugin.
The plugin ships no browser acceptance script; the migration's own web probe still followed the card (token URL -> cookie -> __DSH_BOOT__.entries -> combo bundle).
No userQuestions answerer registration.
No agent-preset inference and no agent-presets roots override.
No isTokenDelta import, first-token detection or TPS computation.
The bundle patch inserts only its own row; it does not reuse or restate the dsh-base composition (no telemetry or package-inventory rows).
No direct @earendil-works/pi-ai dependency or provider/auth plugin code.
dsh-client-runtime is gone from peerDependencies and dsh.client; the browser half is the classic-script __ModuleLoader__ bundle typed against @deepseek-ai/cordis.
Bundle registration id, Loader row name and package.json name all agree on @bench/dsh-bench-mcpanel; verified in the boot manifest and over the /plugins/??@bench/dsh-bench-mcpanel/client.js route.
No session timeline or user-message content reads.
No composer DOM manipulation (draft injection, history recall, shortcuts, selection).
No MarkdownText or fenced CodeBlock render in the shipped client artifact.
No ctx.connection.api, history or transcript reads.
No subagent seed/persisted descriptors.
No ctx.workspaces navigation calls or directory UI.
No third-party persisted SessionEvents, so no ignorable marker to restore.
No unary Remote calls; the panel uses its own webServer routes and connection gate.

Peer cohort declared as the exact published target versions (cordis 4.0.2 + dsh-* 0.1.2-alpha.2, the same tree the shipped 0.1.2-alpha.2 CLI resolves to) with an overrides block holding the transitively auto-installed dsh-* closure on that cohort, so an unfiltered npm install cannot drift onto 0.1.2-rc.1 and the date-bounded cohort install succeeds; the packed tarball still carries only README.md, client.js, cordis.patch.yml, index.js and package.json.
No startup wrapper or Node-22-forcing workaround; the web probe ran on Node 24.21.0, outside the 24.0-24.11.1 failure window.
The plugin does not consume pluginInventory/list or any PluginInventorySnapshot.
No host.describe or ctx.remote.$host usage.
The bundle mounts no dsh-tool-*/dsh-agent* packages and does not compose its own profile; users boot the shipped bundles that already mount session-projection.
No ctx.settings namespace registration, read or write; row state lives in the profile patch layer.
